clue.text: Water falling from roof or tap

definitions.meaning: the original sense of the word: rainwater dripping off the eaves of a building
to tap a phone line is to listen in secretly on a conversation

explanation.walkthrough: The verb sense of listening in grew from standing under the eaves to overhear what was said inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are dictionary meanings: dripping rainwater from the eaves, and covert listening such as a wiretap.

clue.text: Attitude of model wearing messy hose

indicators.note: wearing means the anagrammed hose is put on around the model letter
messy means the letters of hose are jumbled

parts.note: the Model T Ford gives T

explanation.surface: A fashion model in tangled tights has a certain air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'messy' turns HOSE into EHOS, which is worn around T.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethos is the characteristic spirit or attitude of a person or group.

clue.text: Philistine versus empty-headed European

indicators.note: empty-headed means the European word loses its first letter

parts.note: a Bulgarian is a European

explanation.surface: An uncultured person takes on a brainless continental.
explanation.definitionFit: A vulgarian is a coarse, uncultured person, a synonym for a philistine.

clue.text: Criticism swamps argument for covert weapon

indicators.note: swamps means the criticism word engulfs the argument

parts.note: to give someone stick is to criticise them
to have words is to argue

explanation.surface: Fierce criticism overwhelms a debate about a hidden weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A sword concealed inside a walking stick is a covert weapon.

clue.text: Sally makes love with good man in perfect surroundings

indicators.note: in perfect surroundings means the ripe word encloses the other pieces

parts.note: ripe means at its best, perfect
love is zero in tennis, O
ST, saint, is a good man

explanation.surface: A girl called Sally makes love with a decent man in an ideal setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' is not a girl but a witty remark.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally is a quick witty retort, which is what a riposte is.

clue.text: Hand gets praise when trapped in mine

indicators.note: when trapped in means the praise word sits inside the mine word

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
to laud is to praise

explanation.surface: A miner receives praise after being trapped underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'praise' looks like the definition but is the wordplay; 'Hand' is applause, as in give them a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaudit is applause, and giving someone a hand means clapping them.

clue.text: Fine pair of monkeys

definitions.meaning: splendid or excellent, as in a fine old house
in British slang a monkey is five hundred pounds, so two make a thousand

explanation.walkthrough: MONKEY is British slang for £500; GRAND is slang for £1,000, so two monkeys make one.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand means splendid, a synonym of fine, and is also slang for a thousand pounds.

clue.text: Student with information about valley

indicators.note: about means the information word goes around the student letter

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
L is a learner driver's plate, a student

explanation.surface: A student has details about a valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A glen is a narrow valley, especially in Scotland.

clue.text: A warrant keeps regiment on its toes

indicators.note: keeps means the warrant word holds the regiment letter

parts.note: to warrant is to permit, let
R is the abbreviation for regiment

explanation.surface: An order keeps a regiment ready for action.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on one's toes means vigilant and ready, a synonym of alert.

clue.text: Stop fellow becoming cleaner

parts.note: to deter is to stop or discourage
gent is a man, a fellow

explanation.surface: Prevent a chap from turning into a cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: A detergent is a cleaning agent, so cleaner is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Greeting Oscar after trial

indicators.note: after places the Oscar letter behind the trial word

parts.note: an ordeal or trial can be described as hell
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone greets an Academy Award winner after a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word is the standard greeting said on meeting someone.

clue.text: Exercise about to stiffen soldiers' disposition

indicators.note: about means the exercise letters go around the other pieces

parts.note: PT is physical training, school exercise
to lace a drink is to fortify or stiffen it with spirits
soldiers are men, the possessive adding nothing

explanation.surface: A drill is about hardening troops' attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to stiffen' is lacing a drink with alcohol, not starch.
explanation.definitionFit: Disposition here means arrangement or positioning, as in the placement of troops.

clue.text: Allow a team to give way

parts.note: to stand something is to tolerate or allow it
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: Letting a team concede.
explanation.definitionFit: To step out of the way for someone, yielding position, is an idiomatic synonym for giving way.

clue.text: Teacher has time in jail

indicators.note: has means the teacher word holds the time letter inside it

parts.note: pupils address a male teacher as sir

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster has served a prison sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for prison, as in being in stir.

clue.text: Deputy seaman often found on watch

parts.note: a second is an assistant or deputy, as in a duel
a hand is a crew member on a ship

explanation.surface: A deputy sailor is frequently on watch duty at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'watch' is a timepiece, not a sailor's spell of duty.
explanation.definitionFit: The thin pointer counting seconds is a feature of many watch faces.

clue.text: The silt ruined the plant

indicators.note: ruined means the letters of the fodder are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: Silt has spoiled a garden plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A prickly flowering plant, Scotland's national emblem, is an example of a plant.

clue.text: Give money to county officers

parts.note: to tip a waiter is to give money to them
Staffs is the abbreviation for Staffordshire, an English county

explanation.surface: Gratuities for local council officials.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipstaffs are court officers who carry a staff of office.

clue.text: Experience fear as Mike interrupts singer

indicators.note: interrupts means the Mike letter breaks into the singer word

parts.note: a treble is a boy soprano singer
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A frightened performer is cut off mid-song by someone named Mike.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaking with fear is a direct way of experiencing it, so the verb serves as a synonym phrase.

clue.text: Indian dish's extra in the United States

parts.note: a balti is a curry dish, the possessive adding nothing
more means extra

explanation.surface: An additional curry is served across America.
explanation.definitionFit: Baltimore is a city in Maryland, so it lies in the United States.

clue.text: Criticise a guerrilla for dashing style

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly
Che Guevara, the famous guerrilla leader

explanation.surface: Reviewers knock a revolutionary for his flamboyant manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache is flamboyant confidence, a synonym for a dashing style.

clue.text: Raise bone Len broke

indicators.note: broke means the letters of bone and Len are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: Len snapped a bone and needs lifting.
explanation.definitionFit: To ennoble is to raise someone to the nobility.

clue.text: Charter permitted pamphlet

parts.note: to book or charter a plane is to reserve it
let means allowed or permitted

explanation.surface: An authorised charter leaflet.
explanation.definitionFit: A small bound paper of a few pages is a synonym for a pamphlet.

clue.text: Fling mud in bar being upset

indicators.note: in means the mud word sits inside the turned bar word
being upset in a down clue means the bar word is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: a pub is a bar
ooze is soft wet mud

explanation.surface: Someone flings mud in a pub while upset.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'being upset' means the word is turned upside down, so read from bottom to top; BOOZE-UP is British slang for a drinking session.
explanation.definitionFit: A fling is a wild spell of indulgence, and a drinking session is one.

clue.text: Instant credit

definitions.meaning: a moment, as in I'll be with you in a ...

explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British senses: a moment of time, and goods bought on credit.

clue.text: Fret when hot in bistro

indicators.note: in means the hot letter goes inside the bistro word

parts.note: a bistro is a small café
H is the abbreviation for hot, on taps

explanation.surface: Someone frets when it gets hot in the restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: To chafe is to be irritated or impatient, a synonym of fret.

clue.text: Where one enjoys porridge that's healthy

definitions.meaning: porridge is British slang for prison time and the nick is prison, so a pleasant prison would be a good one
in sound condition, in fine shape

explanation.walkthrough: PORRIDGE is British slang for a prison sentence and NICK for a prison; the phrase normally means in good condition.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in good condition, which fits healthy, and literally reads as being inside a fine prison.

clue.text: Deferred to knight holding half-nelson

indicators.note: holding means the knight letters grip the other piece
half signals taking only the first half of the word nelson that follows it

explanation.surface: A knight submits while held in a wrestling hold.
explanation.walkthrough: A half-nelson is a wrestling hold, but here it means half of NELSON.
explanation.definitionFit: Kneeling before someone shows deference, so knelt means deferred to.

clue.text: Precious stone for old crony

parts.note: a pal is a friend or crony

explanation.surface: A gem for an old friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Opal is a gemstone, an example of a precious stone.

clue.text: Northerner caught in lie is nervous

indicators.note: caught in means the northerner is held inside the lie word

parts.note: a fable is an untrue story, a lie
a Lapp is someone from Lapland, in the far north of Europe

explanation.surface: A man from the north is caught out lying and gets anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: Easily agitated or flustered, which is what nervous describes.

clue.text: Notice decoration of brick

parts.note: an ad, advertisement, is a public notice
the OBE is a British honour, Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: An announcement of an award made of brick.
explanation.definitionFit: Adobe is sun-dried clay brick, so brick is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Merchandise keeps wife smart

indicators.note: keeps means the selling word holds the wife letter inside

parts.note: to merchandise goods is to sell them

explanation.surface: Goods for sale keep a wife well dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Swell is dated informal for fashionable or stylish, a synonym of smart.

clue.text: Having mark removed from old gable is appropriate

parts.note: ex means former or old

indicators.note: removed from tells you to take the mark letter out of the gable word

parts.note: a pediment is the triangular gable over a classical portico
M is the abbreviation for the German mark

explanation.surface: An old gable stripped of its markings is fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having' is a link word. PEDIMENT minus M leaves PEDIENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Expedient means suitable or advantageous; with 'is' kept as the definition covers the predicate sense of being appropriate.
